candidates.title: Lipschitz regularity in Flow Matching and Diffusion Models: sharp sampling rates and functional inequalities
candidates.abstract_summary: Establishes sharp Lipschitz regularity for FM vector fields and diffusion scores, with optimal time/dimension dependence and Euler sampler rates around sqrt(d)/N up to logs.
candidates.why_it_may_help: The seed profile explicitly cares about velocity regularity, terminal-time behavior, dimension dependence, and avoiding bad Lipschitz constants.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Try to transfer one-sided/sharp Lipschitz regularity arguments to Student-t priors, mirror-map dual spaces, or Riemannian FM.
candidates.risk: May rely on Euclidean or Gaussian assumptions that do not survive mirror or manifold transformations.
candidates.notes: Strongest innovation lead for constants and sharp discretization rates.

candidates.title: The probability flow ODE is provably fast
candidates.abstract_summary: Proves polynomial-time guarantees for probability-flow ODE sampling, using deterministic dynamics plus a corrector step to handle noncontractive behavior.
candidates.why_it_may_help: It attacks deterministic generative ODE convergence without simple contractivity, which is also a core bottleneck in FM sampler theory.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Investigate whether a corrector or hybrid step can reduce exponential dependence in FM/mirror/RFM discretization analysis.
candidates.risk: The corrector step changes the algorithm and may conflict with purely deterministic flow matching goals.

candidates.title: On the Convergence and Straightness of Rectified Flow
candidates.abstract_summary: Introduces a piecewise-straightness parameter linking path geometry to Wasserstein discretization error and one-step sampling behavior.
candidates.why_it_may_help: The seed papers analyze discretization via regularity constants; this suggests an alternative path-geometry quantity that may better explain solver efficiency.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Define a geometry-aware straightness or curvature-of-path parameter for mirror/Riemannian flow matching.
candidates.risk: Rectified Flow assumptions may not transfer directly to manifold geodesic interpolation or constrained mirror spaces.
candidates.notes: Strong abstraction lead for reframing discretization error.

candidates.title: Flow Matching Generalizes Through Discretization Bias
candidates.abstract_summary: Argues that discretization error itself can induce useful projection-like generalization effects in flow matching, particularly for empirical velocity fields.
candidates.why_it_may_help: The seed profile treats discretization as error; this paper suggests discretization may also be an implicit regularizer or projection mechanism.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Ask whether constrained/geometric FM can exploit discretization bias to improve feasibility or manifold concentration rather than only minimize it.
candidates.risk: Under-review status and empirical-velocity setup make transfer speculative.

candidates.title: Polynomial Convergence of Riemannian Diffusion Models
candidates.abstract_summary: Strengthens Riemannian diffusion theory by proving polynomial step-size guarantees in TV under L2 score accuracy and mild curvature assumptions.
candidates.why_it_may_help: Its TV, curvature, and L2-accuracy machinery may transfer to Riemannian flow matching or provide a benchmark for assumptions.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Compare TV proof tools for Riemannian diffusion and RFM, especially heat-kernel/log-gradient methods versus continuity-equation methods.
candidates.risk: Diffusion proofs use heat-kernel machinery not present in deterministic FM.

candidates.title: Neural Approximate Mirror Maps for Constrained Diffusion Models
candidates.abstract_summary: Learns approximate mirror maps and inverse maps from differentiable distance functions, making mirror-space constrained generation flexible across constraint types.
candidates.why_it_may_help: The mirror FM seed relies on an analytic regularized mirror map; learned mirror maps could widen the constraint classes.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Develop mirror flow matching with neural approximate mirror maps and analyze how approximation error enters dual-to-primal guarantees.
candidates.risk: Theory may become difficult because learned maps may not preserve strong convexity, tail control, or clean metric transfer.
candidates.notes: Useful if the project moves from proof-pattern mining to method design.

candidates.title: Gauge Flow Matching: Efficient Constrained Generative Modeling over General Convex Set and Beyond
candidates.abstract_summary: Uses bijective gauge mappings to reduce generation on compact convex sets to generation on the unit ball, with strict constraint satisfaction and bounded approximation errors.
candidates.why_it_may_help: Offers an alternative to mirror maps and reflection for constrained generation, potentially avoiding some heavy-tail dual-space pathologies.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Compare gauge maps and regularized mirror maps as two transformation-based routes; look for a unifying dual-space guarantee.
candidates.risk: May be more algorithmic than proof-pattern rich; bounded approximation errors need careful reading.
candidates.notes: Strong method innovation lead for constrained domains.

candidates.title: Geometry-Grounded Flow Matching on Compact Manifolds
candidates.abstract_summary: Gives end-to-end Wasserstein guarantees for RFM on compact manifolds, separating statistical, approximation/optimization, and solver errors with intrinsic-dimension learning rates.
candidates.why_it_may_help: Complements the seed TV-rate paper by adding statistical learning and intrinsic dimension components.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Synthesize TV-rate and Wasserstein/statistical-rate frameworks into a fuller RFM error decomposition.
candidates.risk: Workshop paper; compact-manifold focus may not address Hadamard/SPD or heavy-tail issues.
candidates.notes: Strong direct lead for cross-paper skill synthesis.

candidates.title: Generative Modeling with Continuous Flows: Sample Complexity of Flow Matching
candidates.abstract_summary: Analyzes sample complexity for flow matching without assuming access to an ERM, decomposing velocity estimation into neural approximation, statistical, and optimization errors.
candidates.why_it_may_help: The seed profile assumes epsilon-accurate learned fields; this paper studies how that epsilon may arise from learning.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Attach a learning-theoretic front-end to geometric FM error bounds, replacing assumed epsilon accuracy with sample/optimization complexity.
candidates.risk: Under review and bounded-distribution assumptions may limit direct applicability.
candidates.notes: Useful if extending beyond sampler analysis into full end-to-end learning guarantees.

candidates.title: Are We Really Learning the Score Function? Reinterpreting Diffusion Models Through Wasserstein Gradient Flow Matching
candidates.abstract_summary: Reinterprets diffusion training as flow matching to a Wasserstein gradient-flow velocity field rather than exact score learning, emphasizing non-conservative neural fields.
candidates.why_it_may_help: May broaden the conceptual frame from score accuracy to velocity-field transport accuracy, relevant to both diffusion and FM analyses.
candidates.possible_research_angle: Use Wasserstein-gradient-flow language to compare FM, probability-flow ODEs, and Riemannian/geometric samplers.
candidates.risk: May be more conceptual and less directly tied to nonasymptotic discretization proofs.
